Made by Gordon MacLean

↳ Posted by fiel on October 9th, 2003.

This has become a session favourite in Cape Breton. You can hear it on Brenda Stubbert’s CD “Some Tasty Tunes”.

↳ Posted by DonaldK on March 20th, 2007.

http://www.cranfordpub.com/tunes/CapeBreton/Mortgage_Burn.htm

↳ Posted by domhnall. on September 20th, 2007.

I recorded this tune in a session in London a few weeks ago. I only managed to record the last time through and that is what the dots are based on so I can’t be sure that it was played the same everytime through.

No one there knew what it was called, and no one that I’ve played it to since has known it either. Any ideas?

↳ Posted by Hurlock on April 1st, 2009.

it’s Mortgage Burn
https://thesession.org/tunes/2047

↳ Posted by Matt Seattle on April 1st, 2009.

The Mortgage Burn

Becoming very popular in Ireland these days. Please call it The Mortgage Burn as the composer intended it to be called. ‘Mortgage burning is a twentieth-century American custom that is the ritual burning of a paid off mortgage document by homeowners. It is done as a celebratory event, and is sometimes accompanied by a party in which extended family and friends are invited.’(Wikipedia) That’s the idea.

↳ Posted by Christmas Eve on January 5th, 2014.

The Mortgage Burn

Good tune. I’m laughing though, because I’ve always assumed that it was about a small river!

I’ve just had the pleasure of meeting Gordon MacLean the man who ‘made’ this tune! He was playing piano at John Donald Cameron’s ceilidh in Judique, Cape Breton tonight. Lives nearby. An honour, a pleasure- and a humdinging tune to boot!
